sources.title: P. J. Bickel, F. Götze, and W. R. van Zwet, Resampling Fewer Than n Observations: Gains, Losses, and Remedies for Losses
sources.locator: Complete 31-page paper; inspected §2.3 Examples 3–6 (PDF pp. 4–7), §3 definitions and Theorems 1–2 (PDF pp. 8–12), §§4–6 on expansion and extrapolation limits (PDF pp. 13–20), and the Appendix proof of Theorem 2 and its Example 3 check (PDF pp. 26–28).

contents.name: §2.3 Example 3: bootstrap failure for a finite support endpoint

§2.3 Example 6: nondifferentiable absolute-mean functional at zero
§3 definitions of n/n, m/n, without-replacement, and sample-splitting procedures
§3 Theorems 1–2 and their general regularity/tie conditions
contents.reason: The pair proves the uniform-endpoint replacement and nonreplacement cases directly and states the general root-law conditions separately; it does not claim Bickel–Götze–van Zwet's broader theorem for arbitrary statistics.

contents.name: §4–5 higher-order expansions and extrapolation
contents.reason: No extrapolation estimator or accuracy claim is authored here; the page retains the requirement of a separately proved source-specific regular expansion and its remainder regime.

contents.name: Appendix proof of Theorem 2 and its Example 3 endpoint verification
contents.reason: The broad theorem proof is not imported as a substitute for the local proof; the assigned uniform-endpoint result is proved by an exact order-statistic and subset-count argument.

contents.name: §6 extrapolation behavior when the ordinary bootstrap is inconsistent
contents.reason: The source states no general extrapolation validity for irregular problems; this pair makes no such claim and only preserves the warning that regular expansions are required.

web_read_evidence.method: Opened the complete PDF text and read the full assigned endpoint, degenerate-statistic, nondifferentiability, m/n, proof, and extrapolation-limit passages.

contents.reason: This pair states and proves a sufficient uniform-coverage criterion and a separate Bernoulli counterexample; it does not claim the source's general converse theorem for every root class.
